newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's blue-chip firms pull up bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's blue-chip firms pull up bourse higher.

text.p: Morocco's stock exchange closed 0.20 percent higher on Wednesday, due mainly to ONA group and oil refinery Samir, which gained ground, stockbrokers said.
The Casablanca bourse all-share index closed at 640.81 points from 639.54 points on Tuesday.
"The bourse index was up on Wednesday, but traded volumes were low...There is a wait-and-see attitude ahead of new flotations," a broker at BMCI Securities said.
ONA rose five dirhams to 790 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement was up two dirhams at 730 dirhams.
In the energy sector, oil refinery Samir advanced five dirhams to 350 dirhams.
In banking, Banque Commerciale du Maroc gained eight to 868 dirhams.
Also moving ahead, were steel maker Longometal, up seven dirhams at 308 dirhams and truck company Berliet, up eight dirhams at 158 dirhams.
"People are more cautious...They are positioning themselves on small capitalisation firms that are unlikely to drop or increase sharply," the broker said.
Among bad performers was Societe Cherifienne des Petroles, which fell 21 dirhams to 704 dirhams.

SCP, which was recently privatised, showed a net profit of 134 million dirhams for calendar 1996, the company said in a statement. The statement, released Wednesday, showed net profit had risen by 67.5 percent over the 80 million dirham net consolidated profit of 1995.
First tranche of privatisation bonds, issued in January 1996 edged down one dirham to 1,399 dirhams, with 1,172 shares traded.
Credor edged down two dirhams to 745 dirhams.

Total volume traded on the official market was 26.6 million dirhams, down from 41.3 million over the previous session. On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 29.8 million dirhams. The major trade was in 6,716 Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur.
